items.q: Each of these is listed against 'functional proteinuria' in the levels table EXCEPT:
items.exp: The 150–500 mg/day row reads: Functional proteinuria — stress, anxiety, menses, protein supplements; fever is not printed there (it belongs to the febrile proteinuria teaching elsewhere). (Book p744)

items.q: A 24-hour urinary albumin of 450 mg falls into which row of the albumin table?
items.exp: Urinary albumin rows: <30 normal, 30–300 microalbuminuria (moderately elevated albumin in urine), >300 albuminuria. The 150–500 band is the total-protein table, not the albumin table. (Book p744)

items.q: Match each numbered test with what it measures — 1) Test 1 2) Test 2 3) Test 3 … A) Spot urine albumin–creatinine ratio B) Spot urine protein–creatinine ratio C) 24 hour urine protein D) Qualitative dipstick reading
items.exp: The list is 1. 24 hour urine protein, 2. spot urine protein–creatinine ratio (PCR), 3. spot urine albumin–creatinine ratio (ACR), 4. urine dipstick test. (Book p744)

items.q: Fill up: The urine dipstick test for protein is described under 'Tests for proteinuria' as a ______ analysis.
items.exp: Entry 4 reads 'urine dipstick test — qualitative analysis', with the two disadvantages branching from it: positive only around 800 mg and detecting only albumin. (Book p744)

items.q: The flow of injury printed on this page runs albumin → tubular injury → inflammation → TGF-β → fibrosis.
opts: True — fibrosis is the terminal arrow of the chain
False — the chain ends at inflammation
False — TGF-β precedes tubular injury in the printed order
True — but the chain starts with protein, not albumin
items.exp: 'Albumin levels' section: Albumin → Tubular injury → Inflammation → TGF-β → Fibrosis; this is why even moderately elevated albumin requires further evaluation. (Book p744)
